patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Five9 and Vonage share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Five9 only if your buying job matches “Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital from $119/concurrent seat/mo; Core $159; Plus/Pro/E” rather than Vonage's shape. Choose Vonage only if your buying job matches “SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo; Premium/” rather than Five9's shape. Workflow advantage: Five9 leans contact-center, customer-messaging; Vonage leans business-phone, team-communication. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Five9 and Vonage share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Five9 is Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital from $119/concurrent seat/mo; Core $159; Plus/Pro/Enterprise quote — 50-seat minimum.; Vonage is SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo; Premium/Advanced higher..
- Company-size focus: Five9 (mid-market, enterprise) vs Vonage (solo, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Five9-leaning contact-center, customer-messaging vs Vonage-leaning business-phone, team-communication.
- Researched limits: Five9 — 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers; Vonage — Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors.

Limitations — Five9: 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers; Digital is non-voice; Core is the published voice+digital entry; Vonage: Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors; Call recording and deeper CRM land on Advanced / Premium packaging.

Poor-fit cases: Five9 is a poor fit when that limitation bites: 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers · Vonage is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors · Avoid Five9 if you actually need Vonage's motion (SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
